title: Per-tenant allowlist fuses with hedged-shim quarantines and SLO-aware soft trips
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background:
We frequently observe cascading degradations when a single dependency/model for some tenants exhibits increased latency or error bursts. Current hard-trip circuits are blunt instruments: they either fully cut traffic (too aggressive) or allow noisy dependencies to continue degrading other tenants. We need a pluggable, SLO-aware fuse that supports per-tenant allowlists (trusted fallbacks), short-lived hedged shims for graceful detection, quarantine windows, and soft-trip behavior that maintains safety while minimizing user-visible errors.

Goals:
- Provide per-tenant and per-model fuse policies that can operate at multiple scopes (global, region, tenant, model variant).
- Fuse decisions should be SLO-aligned: trips consider p95 latency, error-rate, and SLO burn rate over adaptive windows.
- On a soft-trip, automatically route degraded requests to pre-approved fallback variants or shadow them for canary scoring before full diversion.
- Implement a hedged-shim probe: a lightweight parallel probe to the dependency to verify health before committing a fallback permanently.
- Quarantine failing dependency/tenant combos for a configurable cooldown with progressive backoff and rejoin probes.
- Provide observability: per-tenant trip reasons, timeline, traffic split, cost delta, and canary quality metrics.

Design summary:
- Policy model: JSON policy with scope, thresholds (latency p95, error rate %, SLO burn rate), allowlist of fallback models/regions, quarantine window settings, and hedged-shim parameters (probe timeout, sample rate).
- Decision engine: streaming sliding windows (short/medium/long) compute indicators; Bayesian smoothing to avoid reacting to single spikes. Soft-trip triggers when combined risk score > threshold.
- Hedged-shim: when a soft-trip is triggered, we run a probe to a fallback variant for a small sample of requests and compare output similarity and latency. If probe indicates acceptable quality, shift X% traffic to fallback immediately and continue canarying.
- Quarantine: record trip events per (tenant,dependency,region). While quarantined, automated rejoin probes run at exponential intervals.
- Safety: always preserve a small shadowing sample to capture rare regressions and fail open thresholds. Fall back to hosted-stable variant if no allowlist entry exists.

Acceptance criteria:
1) New policy API implemented and validated with unit + integration tests.
2) Decision engine returns consistent trip/no-trip decisions against synthetic traffic (test harness) with expected sensitivity curves.
3) Hedged-shim probes correctly sample traffic, record similarity metrics, and cause safe progressive traffic shift.
4) Quarantine and rejoin logic operate with exponential backoff and leave clear audit trail.
5) Console surfaces per-tenant trip timeline, sample logs, and canary quality dashboard.
6) Pilot rolled out to two internal tenants and one external low-risk customer with monitoring for 72h without regressions.

Non-goals:
- This ticket is not implementing cross-region automated model replication; it relies on pre-provisioned fallbacks.
- Not addressing long-term ML quality drift detection beyond canary scoring for this iteration.
